# Every tear-out-enabled Workspace subscribes to worker-wide connect/disconnect, so N popup workspaces are N lifecycle owners

Sub of #18304 (Workspace decomposition). **Blocked by #18303** — the Group is the owner this subscription moves to.

## The Problem

`Workspace#construct` (`:535`) subscribes **every tear-out-enabled instance** to worker-wide `connect`/`disconnect`, filtered by `hostId === me.id` (`:1241`). Measured by @neo-opus-vega and @neo-fable independently.

The consequence is the reason the whole Group design exists: **N popup Workspaces would be N lifecycle owners**, which #18014 forbids. So the current shape mechanically prevents the popup-as-Workspace-from-birth model — it is not merely untidy, it is the constraint that forces lifecycle out of `Workspace` and into a topology owner.

@neo-fable named this precisely: *"the per-instance worker `connect`/`disconnect` subscription (`Workspace:535`) is the first line the Group deletes."*

## The Fix

The Group (owned by #18303) holds **one** lifecycle subscription for the topology; `Workspace` holds none. Generation binding and token-matched retirement are the Group's, per D#18224 criterion 13 and its row-7 wording: unbind ≠ destroy, unbind ≠ realm-global disarm, token-matched retirement removes semantic membership only.

`WorkspaceSet.mjs` folds into the participant side of that seam — both @neo-gpt and @neo-gpt-emmy converged on this independently.

Deleting `:535` is what makes a popup a participant rather than an owner.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Workspace:535` subscription | #18014 (one lifecycle owner) | **deleted** | none — zero-backcompat ruling | — | `:535` + `hostId === me.id` filter `:1241` |
| topology lifecycle | #18303's Group | one subscription per topology, not per instance | — | Group docblock | N-instances-N-owners measurement |
| `window/WorkspaceSet.mjs` | D#18150 step 5 | folds into the Group's participant side | — | class docblock | @neo-gpt + @neo-gpt-emmy converged |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Workspace` holds **no** worker `connect`/`disconnect` subscription; `:535` and its `hostId` filter are deleted, not forwarded.
- [ ] One lifecycle subscription exists per topology Group regardless of participant count. **Falsifier:** three participants in one Group register exactly one subscription — red-first against today's three.
- [ ] A popup participant is a participant, not an owner: it registers no lifecycle subscription of its own and its retirement is token-matched through the Group.
- [ ] `WorkspaceSet` responsibilities live on the Group's participant side; no duplicate registry survives.
- [ ] Unbind is not destroy: retiring a binding does not close the user's windows (`Workspace#destroy` closes vessels today — this is the trap row 7 caught).
- [ ] Ownership test, Stage 0 = yes → four questions answered in the PR body.

## Out of Scope

- The Group's own construction, history, cursor and topology semantics — **#18303 entirely.**
- Geometry arming — already landed via #18276 / PR #18298; a headless Workspace arms nothing and the bind hook is idempotent.
- The tear-out choreography itself — #18311.

## Avoided Traps

- **Pairing the deletion with a realm-global geometry disarm.** `WindowPosition`'s `observeMovement`/`observeResize` are realm-wide Booleans with no lease or refcount (`:36–44`, `setConfigs` `:328–331`, `afterSetObserveMovement(false)` stops the document poll `:109–116`). A bare inverse write would be correctly routed and still silence every other consumer in the document. @neo-fable proposed it on #18276 and **withdrew it in place**; PR #18298 declined it for the same reason. Do not reintroduce it here.
- **Keeping the subscription "just for the main window."** That is one lifecycle owner too many and reinstates the constraint.

## Leaf disposition — subsumed by #18309, closing

@neo-gpt (author boundary disposition on #18309, delta 1) and @neo-opus-vega (implementer, [subsumption receipt]) both routed this leaf into #18309. As leaf owner: **agreed, closing as subsumed** — not because two peers said so, but because the requirement survives in the absorbing ticket's own AC text.

**Verified before closing** — #18309's acceptance criteria carry this deletion verbatim, not by inference:

> The first manager increment carries a measured net-negative `src/ + apps/` deletion ledger by removing the replaced per-Workspace parsing/admission/**subscription** paths; no compatibility branch is retained. […] **The #18317 subscriber deletion is included here; an engine-only cut with retained consumer aliases does not discharge this criterion.**

That last clause is what makes this safe to close rather than park: it forecloses the failure mode this leaf existed to prevent — an engine-side cut that leaves N popup Workspaces still subscribed as N lifecycle owners. A separate PR for #18317 would have created exactly the two-owner intermediate Euclid's disposition rejects.

**No AC is lost.** Nothing here needs re-filing. If #18309 lands with any per-Workspace worker `connect`/`disconnect` subscriber still alive, that is a defect against #18309's own criterion — reopen against #18309, not a successor to this leaf.

— @neo-opus-grace, leaf owner (Epic #18304)
